rationale: Both are the local speech path for the iMessage thread on the Mac mini: they need the same kind of Homebrew installs (whisper.cpp and ffmpeg for transcription; ffmpeg and a speech engine for the later neural voice) and are tied together by one setting, tts.auto "inbound", which sends an audio reply only after a voice memo, and the roadmap lists local transcription in and local audio replies out as one 'Voice (iMessage)' component. VOX-04's wave C has no later dependency behind it (it needs only F003, and its first step is the built-in say voice with no install), neither half adds an agent or a way to send data out, and the card keeps F003's medium risk, the open check that the audio file itself stays off the cloud model, and the rule that the Microsoft online voice is switched off.
name: Voice by iMessage, kept on the Mac mini: voice memos transcribed locally, spoken replies in a local voice (macOS say first, a neural voice later, cloud speech switched off)

rationale: Both are prompt programs in the same per-person AGENTS.md on the parent's own agent and run on the same input (a pasted text, photo or PDF read through F002): the first returns the five lines with the dates and the deadline, the second offers reminders for those same dates and writes nothing until the parent says yes. F011's wave B has no dependency behind it for the reminder half (its own record says that half needs only attachment reading and F007, both wave A), the calendar-entry offer stays with F010 on its own high-risk card, and the merged card carries F011's medium risk because an agreed reminder is a write.
name: Explain this, then offer reminders: a document, school message, flyer, homework concept or how-to in five lines, with the dates it finds proposed as reminders after a yes

rationale: Both are answer recipes for the one memory-less research agent, reached by the same hand-off from the parent's agent: it reads public pages and returns a short list of options with links, giving a price, hours or dates only where a tool result shows them, and the parent does the buying or booking. Both are wave C and low risk with no payment or booking tool, and the card names the two things only the outing half uses: the Places lookup (F021, which stays its own card because it needs a Google key with billing on) and the Friday job, which passes calendar free time to research as date ranges only.
name: Options research with sourced links: products, camps and programmes, day outings and trips (parents buy and book)

rationale: Both turn dinners into items on the shared grocery list through the same last step, an offer that writes to the Reminders list (F030) only after a yes: one starts from a recipe link the parent sends, the other from a Sunday plan of five dinners drawn from the saved recipes, the week's calendar and allergies. F033's wave C has no dependency behind it (calendar read, the Reminders bridge and the household store or vault are all wave A), nothing is ordered in either, and the card states the two parts separately (the research agent reads the recipe page; the Sunday plan is a scheduled job on the parent's own agent that reads the calendar and the saved recipes) and carries F033's medium risk.
name: Meals to the grocery list: recipe link to ingredients and steps, and a Sunday dinner plan with a recipe box

rationale: Both are scheduled, isolated, report-only jobs on the owner's own mail agent, capped to the read-only Gmail tools and announced only to the owner; they differ in the cron line and the prompt (a 07:00 list of mail that needs action, and a Saturday list from January to April of which expected tax forms have had an arrival email). Both are wave C at medium risk and wait on the same open decision about personal mail reaching the cloud model, neither writes a draft, and the card says that the tax checklist reports arrival only and that 'does not read the form' is an instruction to the agent and not an enforced limit.
name: Scheduled reports from each adult's read-only mail agent: 07:00 action digest, and a January-to-April tax-form arrival checklist

rationale: Both are children's paperwork helpers on the parent's own agent built from the same pieces: dated rows in the household store (F031), stored per-child facts, fixed linked rules, and a drafts-only output (a copy-paste answer block for a school or camp form, a consent-letter text for a trip) that the parent signs and submits. Both are wave C at medium risk and Happy fills, certifies, books and sends nothing in either; the card notes the one extra hand-off of the trip half, where the research agent is asked about a country and ages only.
name: Children's paperwork kit: enrolment, camp and health forms, and travel documents before a trip

rationale: Both let the parents check on Happy itself through a short per-adult Sunday text, one listing what it did that week (reminders created, list items added, messages sent, approvals given) and one listing what it saved to memory, so they are one weekly review and should not arrive as two texts on the same evening. Both are wave B and each text goes only to its owner; the card states the operator's forget-a-conversation step as a separate part and carries F085's medium risk.
name: Weekly review of Happy itself: what it did and what it remembered, with forgetting a conversation on request

rationale: All three are the same operator-created host command job with no model: a small script fetches a public source (weather alerts for home, a team calendar link, a site's feed or page, the CPSC and FDA recall lists), keeps seen ids in a state file and prints one templated line or NO_REPLY, and F029 and SRC-03 both list F018's command-job pattern as their dependency. All are wave B and low risk, no agent or model reads the fetched text, and each watch stays its own job to switch on; the home_weather tool (F083) stays a separate card because the briefs and the outing planner also read it, and the calendar conflict watch (MKT-06) stays separate because it reads the parents' own calendars under a new sharing grant.
name: Public-source watchers with no model: storm alerts for home, a moved game or a changed page, and recalls matched to what the family owns
